newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Cook clashes with Serb leader over war crime issue.
newsitem.headline: Cook clashes with Serb leader over war crime issue.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook warned a Bosnian Serb nationalist leader on Tuesday that the international community would not drop demands for the prosecution of suspected war criminals.
Cook and the Serb member of Bosnia's collective presidency, Momcilo Krajisnik, sharply disagreed over the war crimes issue in talks held in the Sarajevo suburb of Lukavica.

"The Dayton (peace) agreement clearly sets out the obligation of the authorities throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and Republika Srpska (Serb republic) to hand over those who have been indicted," Cook told reporters.
"The international community is not going to let this one go and I am confident that one day those who have been indicted will stand trial," he said.
A raid this month by British soldiers on two Serbs indicted for war crimes has angered Krajisnik and other nationalist hardliners who feel threatened by the tougher international approach.
Krajisnik said that calls for extraditing war crimes suspects, including former Bosnian Serb president Radovan Karadzic, were counter-productive and dangerous.
"Emphasising this war crimes issue makes lasting reconciliation in Bosnia-Herzegovina impossible," he told reporters.
Krajisnik said the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague should travel to Bosnia's Serb republic to gain a more "objective" view and hear criticism of the indictments issued against Karadzic.
"In the Serb republic, Mr Karadzic is not considered to be guilty," said Krajisnik, a loyal ally of Karadzic.

The U.N. tribunal has indicted Karadzic for helping orchestrate the brutal siege of Sarajevo, the "ethnic cleansing" -- or mass expulsions -- of Moslems and Croats, and the slaughter of thousands of Moslem men from the eastern enclave of Srebrenica.
Cook said he had "a very frank exchange" with Krajisnik and that the issue of extraditing war criminals dominated the meeting.
The British foreign secretary also told reporters that aid to the Serb entity would be linked to Serb compliance with the 1995 Dayton accords.

The NATO swoop this month broke new ground for the alliance-led peace force, which had previously ruled out arrest operations unless peacekeeping troops encountered suspects during their regular duties.
Western governments decided to change tactics because they say Karadzic and other indicted war criminals continue to wield power behind the scenes and are trying to sabotage the Dayton treaty.

Diplomats have blamed Karadzic loyalists for a wave of retaliatory bombings and other violence following the NATO raid. Two U.S. soldiers and one Dutch soldier have been injured in the revenge attacks.
In a veiled threat, Krajisnik indicated that the more aggressive NATO policy could result in more retaliation.
He said the introduction of sealed, or secret, indictments by the tribunal "disturbs our people a lot".
"Now there are reactions which are not controlled and all of this makes the situation more difficult," Krajisnik said.
Cook was expected to discuss political turmoil in Serb territory in a meeting with Krajisnik's rival, Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic, later on Tuesday.

Plavsic, based in the northwest town of Banja Luka, is locked in a tense power struggle with Karadzic and his allies, whom she accuses of running vast smuggling rackets which discourage foreign reconstruction aid and keep the majority of Serbs in abject poverty.
Plavsic's detailed accusations have helped focus attention on possible corruption in the Moslem-Croat Federation part of Bosnia as well.
Cook said before his trip that he intended to raise the issue of possible misuse of reconstruction aid in his talks with Alija Izetbegovic, the Moslem chairman of the collective presidency.

Izetbegovic responded angrily on Monday to a British newspaper report that post-war aid had been spent improperly. He said he would form a special commission to investigate allegations of fraud but that if the charges proved false, foreigners "spreading such lies" would be deported.
